headline: Goose’s default filesystem and MCP access create medium-to-high risks when paired with a non-runnable knowledge list that can be treated as trusted input.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no runtime surfaces, so it cannot directly ingest B. But B can read/write the filesystem and use MCP, and its outputs may be copied into A’s knowledge-management context manually or via shared files. That makes prompt injection plausible through shared workspace content, though not automatic. Uncertainty about A’s ingestion path pushes this above low.
conditions: IF A is fed B-generated files or notes as trusted content, injection becomes plausible.
IF the pair shares a writable workspace, malicious text in B outputs can reach A indirectly.
mitigations: Keep A and B on separate workspaces.
Strip instructions from any B-generated artifacts before A reads them.
Use a fixed template for A inputs.
Disable MCP sources that can write untrusted text into shared files.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no I/O, while B reads and writes the user filesystem and handles source code/files in cwd. If A’s curated content or B’s working files contain secrets, B can exfiltrate them over broad network egress. The pair therefore has a default leakage path through shared files, even though A itself is not a transmitter.
conditions: IF sensitive material is placed in the shared cwd, B can read it.
IF B is allowed to send context to configured providers, file contents may leave the machine.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared cwd.
Run B in a dedicated directory with minimal files.
Disable network egress for B when handling sensitive work.
Rotate any exposed tokens immediately.
requires-engineering: enforce per-directory access controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A is non-runnable and has no write or network capabilities, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. B can modify git state and write the filesystem, but there is no overlapping write surface from A. The interaction is therefore mostly one-sided, with only a small risk if external orchestration maps A’s outputs into B’s workspace.
conditions: IF an orchestrator writes A outputs into the same git repo B edits, conflicts can occur.
IF B runs multiple instances on the same filesystem, its own shared-state model can collide.
mitigations: Avoid writing A outputs into B’s repo.
Use separate git branches per task.
Run only one B instance per workspace.
Commit or stash before switching tasks.
requires-engineering: add workspace locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a knowledge-management list, so its outputs may be treated as authoritative references. B is a coding agent with shell, git, and MCP actions, so if B consumes A’s curated output without verification, errors can cascade into code or operational changes. The pathway exists in default workflows where lists are reused as source material.
conditions: IF B uses A’s output as a source of truth without checking upstream links, errors propagate.
IF A’s list is copied into tickets or scripts, B may act on stale or incorrect entries.
mitigations: Require B to verify every A-derived claim against primary sources.
Mark A outputs as non-authoritative in task prompts.
Add a review step before shell or git actions.
Limit B to read-only analysis for A-derived tasks.
requires-engineering: implement citation/provenance checks.

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, residency, or retention mismatch is documented for A, and B’s profile only shows source code and cwd files. The main compliance concern is that B handles secrets and broad network egress, but without a documented regulated data class flowing from A, this is a limited gap rather than a breach. A is not cited for a residency issue because none is stated.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into B’s workspace, compliance risk increases.
IF B is used on data subject to stricter retention rules than its providers, policy mismatch can occur.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of B.
Review provider retention settings before use.
Use redacted inputs for compliance-sensitive tasks.
Document allowed data classes for B.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for data residency and retention.
